title: Returned Payments, Returned Payment Fees and Certified Funds on the Apartment Home Lease
content:
A payment on an Apartment Home Lease that the bank or card network dishonors is booked back to the ledger under this standard.

## 1. The return

A returned payment reverses the original payment in full: the return carries the original payment as its source and the original amount, dated the day the bank or card network returned it.

## 2. The returned payment fee

2.1 A return for insufficient funds, account closed or stop payment posts one returned payment fee line for that payment. A card chargeback posts no fee, because a card dispute is the cardholder's right.

2.2 Only one returned payment fee posts for a given returned payment; the check is made against the returned payment fee lines already on the ledger for that same returned payment.

2.3 The fee is the floor plan's company returned payment fee, reduced to the cap of the community's state when that cap is lower. In California the first cap applies to the first fee-bearing return ever recorded on the lease, and the subsequent cap to every later one.

| State of the community | Cap on the first fee-bearing return | Cap on each later fee-bearing return |
|---|---|---|
| California (CA) | $25.00 | $35.00 |
| Washington (WA) | $40.00 | $40.00 |
| Colorado (CO) | $20.00 | $20.00 |
| Texas (TX) | $30.00 | $30.00 |
| Georgia (GA) | $30.00 | $30.00 |
| Arizona (AZ) | $25.00 | $25.00 |

*Hypothetical:* with a company fee of $50.00, the second fee-bearing return on a California lease posts a fee of $35.00, and any fee-bearing return on a Colorado lease posts $20.00. A state cap above the company fee would leave the company fee unchanged.

## 3. Certified funds only

3.1 The count that matters is the number of returns on the lease dated within the trailing 365 days ending on and including the evaluation date whose reason is insufficient funds, account closed or stop payment. When that count, including the return just recorded, reaches the floor plan's trigger count, the lease is placed on certified funds only, with the restriction's last date equal to the return date plus the floor plan's restriction length in calendar months (same day number, falling back to the month's last day), and any autopay enrollment is cancelled the same day.

3.2 The restriction ends by itself after its last date. It is recorded as released at the first ledger action after that date, and it is never shortened on request.

### Dates of a restriction (hypothetical, 12-month restriction)

| Triggering return dated | Last date of the restriction |
|---|---|
| 14 May 2024 | 14 May 2025 |
| 29 February 2024 | 28 February 2025 (no 29 February in 2025, so the month's last day) |

### Points of judgement

- A card chargeback carries no fee and is not a return of the counted kinds.
- A request to lift the restriction early does not shorten it.
